text:
sam: Quick q — when the collector starts rejecting OTLP because downstream exporter is backpressured, what should the SDK sampler do? We're running route-deterministic in the SDK + tail-sampling in the collector. If SDK drops traces early we lose tail signal. Thoughts?

casey: don't drop full traces at SDK for routes where we rely on collector tail-sampling. for very high-volume routes we can deterministic sample at a low rate, but otherwise send.

irina: agreed. we added a lightweight "forward-needed" hint last quarter but it's not wired into SDKs yet. options i see:
- SDK always forwards but uses a minimal envelope (resource + trace_id + root span) to reduce bandwidth
- SDK applies a soft probabilistic head sampler and includes a sampling-hint header for the tail processor
- SDK falls back to a per-tenant quota mode when exporter returns RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED / 429s

sam: what's this "minimal envelope"? is that an OTLP thing or internal?

casey: not standard. proto-wise we'd send a trimmed ExportTraceServiceRequest with only ResourceSpans for the root/span skeleton. rough example of collector config we run: 
```yaml
exporters:
  otlp:
    endpoint: otlp.redwood.internal:4317
processors:
  tail_sampling:
    policies:
      - name: important-tiers
        type: tail_sampling/latency
        decision_wait: 10s
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch, tail_sampling]
      exporters: [otlp]
```

irina: console UX implication — we need a per-route toggle: "always-forward for tail analysis" with an estimated cost shown. also expose a per-tenant "sampling-budget" so when exporter pressure hits we degrade according to budget.

telemetry-bot: collector/tail-sampler v2 deployed to staging @2024-07-18T17:05 :rocket:

mike: implementation idea: negotiation header X-Forward-Hint. collector signals preferred mode in responses. when SDK sees RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED it switches to quota-mode: favor high-SLA tenants, deterministic keep for error routes, probabilistic for best-effort tenants.

casey: i'll draft a short RFC describing: SDK negotiation headers, minimal-envelope wire format, quota-mode rules, and console controls. also add rollout plan: feature-flagged on dev region -> staging -> grad rollout.

sam: SGTM. can someone pick up a small spike to measure bandwidth & latency impact of always-forward minimal envelope for the top 20 routes? we need numbers to show product/finance.

irina: i'll take the spike. will post perf numbers + a sample collector policy and demo console toggle by EOW.

sam: thanks :thumbsup:
